result.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
result.summary: Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together. Across 13 vision-language model and generator pairs, generation lowers mean accuracy by 3.7 percentage points, with declines on nine of ten tasks. Two unified models, BAGEL and Janus-Pro-7B, each lose accuracy on eight tasks. On VSTAR, adding a generated image to the same planning hint lowers accuracy by 10.47 points. Repeated image edits yield different outcomes across tasks. ChartQAPro and MathVista stay below their no-generation baselines, while ERQA gains three points after ten edits.

AI.brief_summary: 论文实证检验「先让模型描述所需辅助图像、再结合原图与生成图作答」能否提升视觉问答：在13组视觉语言模型与生成器配对上评测，平均准确率下降3.7个百分点，10个任务中9个下降；两个统一模型各在8个任务上退步，VSTAR上加入生成图并附相同规划提示反而降10.47点，反复编辑结果因任务而异（ChartQAPro、MathVista仍低于无生成基线，ERQA十次编辑后升3点）。
AI.relevance_reason: 属「以图像思考」的负结果与视觉证据筛选诊断，可供核查显式生成外部辅助图像与内部 latent 视觉推理在收益、成本和编辑次数上的差异。
